evidence.claim: FERC issued Order No. 1920 to require long-term regional transmission planning and cost-allocation reforms, creating a policy catalyst for transmission planning and project pipelines.
evidence.source_title: FERC Takes on Long-Term Planning with Historic Transmission Rule

evidence.claim: FERC's explainer says Order Nos. 1920 and 1920-A direct transmission providers to improve long-term assessment of transmission needs and cost-allocation processes.
evidence.source_title: Explainer on the Transmission Planning and Cost Allocation Final Rule

evidence.claim: EIA forecast U.S. electricity consumption growth of about 2% in both 2025 and 2026, with growth linked to new semiconductor factories, battery manufacturing facilities and data centers.
evidence.source_title: EIA extends five key energy forecasts through December 2026

evidence.claim: DOE states that the United States has limited commercial supplies of HALEU enrichment services available to support advanced reactor deployment.

External search context from Focus on Risk describes Centrus's Piketon HALEU cascade as a Western HALEU bottleneck; this supports a candidate relationship but requires DOE, NRC and company filing validation.
evidence.source_title: The Fuel That Could Strand the Nuclear Renaissance

evidence.claim: External search context from Lanin characterizes PLPC as a transmission hardware supplier with low Wall Street attention and potential specification stickiness; this is useful discovery input but needs primary-source and customer-validation checks.
evidence.source_title: The Only Pure-Play Transmission Hardware Stock Nobody Is Talking About

memory_update.text: For the Energy theme, use PWR and VRT as reference anchors for grid execution and data-center power infrastructure, but do not let them crowd out smaller suppliers in transmission hardware, power packages, magnetics, conduit, engineering services and nuclear fuel-cycle chokepoints.
PSIX, GNRC and similar backup-power names should be evaluated through large-load, C&I and data-center backlog quality rather than residential generator narratives alone.

BELFB and NVT are second-order electrical-component mappings; their survival into later layers requires proof of customer pull from AI/data-center, utility T&D, substation, power-quality or standards-driven applications.

PLPC is a potentially important underfollowed transmission hardware candidate, but current evidence is mostly discovery-level external commentary. Prioritize primary-source validation of product qualification, utility approved-material-list presence, backlog and U.S. transmission exposure.

LEU maps to the nuclear enrichment and HALEU chokepoint, but should remain speculative_shadow until DOE task orders, NRC licensing, commercial volumes, financing and Russian-supply transition risks are validated from primary sources.

Need current market cap, analyst coverage, revenue segment, backlog, book-to-bill, customer concentration and margin bridge for each candidate before assigning underfollowed status with high confidence.

Need primary-source company filings and transcripts for PSIX, WLDN, BELFB, NVT, GNRC, ATKR, PLPC and LEU. Current Layer 2B relationships are mostly hypotheses or inferences derived from Layer 1 candidate mappings plus broad FERC/EIA/DOE demand evidence.

Need falsification checks for each node: data-center interconnection delays turning into cancellations, utility capex slippage, component overcapacity, margin compression from labor/material costs, customer insourcing, failed qualification, or stock rerating ahead of fundamentals.

summary: Mapped public-market ticker relationships for the Energy candidate chunk around U.S. grid scarcity, large-load power demand, backup/dispatchable generation, transmission execution, electrical components, and nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks. Reference leaders are retained as benchmark anchors, while underfollowed names are mapped to second-order or hidden supply-chain nodes requiring primary-source validation before promotion to later Serenity layers.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether data-center product-line ramp costs convert into sustained multi-customer revenue growth and margin recovery rather than one-time backlog pull-forward.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check latest 10-K/10-Q, earnings-call transcript, backlog disclosure, customer concentration, product mix, large-engine capacity, warranty reserves, and gross-margin bridge for data-center or C&I power-system references.
ticker_relationships.node: Dispatchable power equipment, engines, generator sets, standby and prime power packages
ticker_relationships.relationship: Potential second-order beneficiary if data centers, industrial customers, and utilities need faster-to-deploy backup or on-site power while grid interconnection and transmission upgrades lag demand growth.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Electric segment backlog converts into revenue without labor-cost, subcontractor, or acquisition-integration margin leakage.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull latest annual report, segment backlog, book-to-bill, utility customer mix, craft-labor capacity commentary, acquisition details, and project margin disclosures.
ticker_relationships.node: High-voltage transmission construction, specialty utility EPC labor, grid-hardening execution capacity
ticker_relationships.relationship: Reference leader for the utility construction and skilled-labor bottleneck. If FERC-driven transmission planning, data-center load growth, renewables interconnection, and grid-hardening capex accelerate, PWR is the benchmark for how scarce execution capacity is being priced.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether conversion-service pricing, UF6 capacity utilization, restart or expansion spending, and long-term utility contracting add more incremental margin than uranium mining volumes alone.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review Cameco annual report, fuel-services segment disclosure, conversion capacity, long-term contract book, realized prices, JV/fuel-fabrication disclosures, and utility contracting commentary.
ticker_relationships.node: Nuclear fuel cycle: uranium mining, conversion, fuel services and nuclear fuel fabrication exposure
ticker_relationships.relationship: Reference leader for nuclear fuel-cycle exposure. The Serenity relationship is not just uranium mining; the key mapping is whether conversion and fuel-services capacity become more valuable as utilities manage Russian supply restrictions and advanced-reactor fuel needs.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether the APG acquisition or related operations materially increase exposure to data-center, high-load grid interconnection, substation design, backlog, and margins.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify acquired business mix, utility and data-center customer references, backlog, project sizes, APG revenue contribution, gross margin by service line, and whether work is recurring programmatic demand or project-specific.
ticker_relationships.node: Engineering, interconnection support, utility programs, energy services and construction-management capacity
ticker_relationships.relationship: Potential underfollowed engineering-capacity beneficiary where large-load customers and utilities need substation design, interconnection coordination, energy-efficiency programs, and program-management support before physical grid upgrades can proceed.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether bottlenecks in switchgear, busway and integrated power modules are still expanding faster than added capacity, or whether market expectations already discount most growth.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track orders, backlog, capacity additions, Americas versus international data-center exposure, power versus thermal segment growth, lead-time commentary, and hyperscaler concentration.
ticker_relationships.node: Critical digital infrastructure: data-center power conditioning, UPS, busway, switchgear-adjacent systems and thermal management
ticker_relationships.relationship: Reference anchor for the obvious data-center power-quality expression. Useful for benchmarking growth, orders, and margins against smaller electrical-component or power-infrastructure suppliers.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether large networking-customer demand and Magnetic Solutions backlog are tied to AI data-center networking and power architecture, or merely to cyclical networking recovery.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check segment backlog, Magnetic Solutions revenue, customer concentration, design-win language, data-center or networking product references, gross-margin durability, and capex for magnetics capacity.
ticker_relationships.node: Custom magnetics, power conversion components, protection, connectivity and electronic components for higher-density power architectures
ticker_relationships.relationship: Underfollowed component-level candidate. It may benefit one or two steps away from the obvious AI/data-center load driver if networking, industrial, defense, transportation, and e-mobility customers require more reliable magnetics and power-protection components.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine how much revenue comes from utility T&D grounding and bonding, and whether products are specified in approved-material lists or standards such as permanent substation grounding connections.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review product catalogs, utility T&D revenue disclosure, standards certifications, customer vertical mix, substation/renewables/transmission references, and margin resilience versus general industrial electrical demand.
ticker_relationships.node: Electrical connection and protection: utility grounding, bonding, enclosures, connectors and standards-driven substation hardware
ticker_relationships.relationship: Second-order grid hardware candidate. The visible company story is broad electrical connection/protection, but the narrower Serenity mapping is whether its grounding, bonding and connector products are embedded in utility-approved materials and long-life standards-driven applications.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Large-megawatt generator backlog, hyperscaler or data-center customer concentration, capacity expansion, margin profile of C&I/data-center units versus residential standby, and durability beyond one-time backlog build.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Separate residential standby from C&I revenue, check megawatt-scale generator orders, backlog, lead times, channel inventory, data-center customer references, and gross-margin bridge by product family.
ticker_relationships.node: Backup power generation, commercial and industrial generators, large-megawatt standby systems and distributed energy technology
ticker_relationships.relationship: Potential beneficiary of critical-load backup requirements as data centers, hospitals, telecom, industrial facilities and utilities require resilient power even when grid capacity is constrained.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether data-center, utility and industrial demand is large enough to offset PVC and steel price normalization plus cyclical construction weakness.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check volume versus price mix, end-market exposure to data centers/utilities/industrial, distributor inventory, margin normalization, backlog, and commentary from electrical distributors.
ticker_relationships.node: Electrical conduit, fittings, raceway, cable management and installation infrastructure
ticker_relationships.relationship: Second-order electrification and data-center buildout candidate. Even when transformers and switchgear are the headline bottlenecks, large electrical projects require conduit, cable support, fittings and raceway systems, but commodity price normalization can obscure volume growth.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether PLPC is actually embedded in utility specifications and approved-material lists across high-voltage transmission projects, and whether order growth is tied to U.S. grid buildout rather than normal utility maintenance.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate through annual report, segment geography, utility product catalogs, customer concentration, backlog/order commentary, transmission exposure, approved-vendor evidence, and margin impact from metals/input costs.
ticker_relationships.node: Transmission-line hardware, conductor fittings, clamps, connectors and conductor-adjacent components
ticker_relationships.relationship: Underfollowed pure-play style mapping to mandatory transmission bill-of-material hardware. If transmission miles, reconductoring, grid hardening, and advanced-conductor projects increase, PLPC may capture value through qualified hardware specified by utilities and EPCs.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether demonstration HALEU capability can scale into commercial domestic enrichment capacity with financing, customer contracts, regulatory approvals, and supply-chain execution before policy demand shifts or delays.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify DOE task orders, NRC licensing status, Piketon cascade production, SWU and HALEU volumes, capex funding, customer contracts, Russian supply exposure, import-waiver assumptions, and balance-sheet capacity.
ticker_relationships.node: Nuclear fuel cycle: uranium enrichment, HALEU demonstration, domestic enrichment services and SWU supply
ticker_relationships.relationship: Speculative chokepoint candidate for domestic enrichment and HALEU availability. The upside mapping is clear if advanced reactors and U.S. policy require non-Russian enrichment; the risk mapping is equally central because current revenues may depend on legacy enrichment supply relationships and scale-up execution.
